---
name: docs-audit
description: Audit a project's docs against the docs-kit content contract and write a gap report to docs/.audit.md. Use when asked to audit docs, find which docs are missing or stale, check README drift, or produce a docs gap report; files one GitHub issue per gap on request.
---

# docs-audit

Score the consuming project (the current repository) against the content contract: `docs/site.yaml` valid per the kit schema, a Diátaxis page tree under `docs/src/content/docs/` (getting-started, guides, concepts, reference), reference generated by refgen and current, README true to the code. Output is a gap report in the format of [report-format.md](report-format.md); `docs-write` consumes it one gap per run.

Read-only audit: the project tree ends exactly as it started except for `docs/.audit.md`. Builds and generated files go to a temp dir.

Every gap carries evidence: `path:line`, or a command with its decisive output line. A fact you could not check stays in the report prefixed `unverified:`, never dropped and never stated as fact.

## Setup

```sh
KIT="${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../.."   # docs-kit root when the skill runs from the kit or its plugin
RAW=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zebradil/docs-kit/main
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
git rev-parse --short HEAD        # the audited commit, for the report header
```

When `$KIT/schema/site.schema.json` or `$KIT/refgen/help2md.mjs` is missing, download it from `$RAW/<same path>` into `$TMP` and use that copy. Both run without installing anything into the kit.

## Checks

Run all five. Each yields zero or more gaps.

1. **Contract.** `docs/site.yaml` missing is a gap. Present: validate it and turn each error line into an evidence item:
   ```sh
   npx --yes ajv-cli@5.0.0 validate --spec=draft2020 --all-errors --errors=text -s <schema> -d docs/site.yaml
   ```
   Then check each `install[].code` against the build files and README: a command that cannot work is a gap.
2. **Page tree.** Look for `getting-started.md(x)`, `guides/`, `concepts/`, `reference/` under `docs/src/content/docs/`. A section is empty when it has no page, or only pages holding front matter or placeholder text. Plan the pages the project needs, one gap per page: getting-started is one tutorial; guides are one per user task (README sections, CLI commands, workflows); concepts are one per core idea (glossary, `CONTEXT.md`, ADRs, the README's how-it-works prose). Existing docs outside the tree are seed material; cite them in `action`.
3. **Reference.** Build the CLI into `$TMP`: from `reference.cli.build`/`path` in `site.yaml` when present, otherwise `cargo build --target-dir "$TMP/target"` or `go build -o "$TMP/bin/" ./...`, wrapped in `nix develop -c` when the project has a flake devShell. Then:
   ```sh
   node <help2md.mjs> --bin <built binary> --out "$TMP/ref"
   diff -r "$TMP/ref" docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli
   ```
   No committed `reference/cli/` is a gap; any diff is a stale-reference gap (`fix-by: refgen`, evidence: `diff -rq` output). Commands or flags with an empty description in `$TMP/ref` form one low gap (`fix-by: code`) citing each definition in source. When the build fails, read the CLI definitions in source (clap derive or builder, cobra commands), record the build error under Not checked, and prefix reference evidence with `unverified:`.
4. **CLI coverage.** For every command and flag in `$TMP/ref`, search getting-started, guides, and concepts. List each uncovered one in the evidence of the page gap from check 2 that should cover it; open a separate gap only for a command no planned page covers. With no hand-written pages yet, run the search against README and name that stand-in under Not checked.
5. **README drift.** Check every README claim that carries a command, flag, env var, default, number, or path against help output, source, and the file system. A disagreement is a gap citing both sides (`README.md:<line>` and `<source>:<line>`); an agreement leaves no trace.

A project with no docs-kit setup (no `site.yaml` and no page tree) gets one `fix-by: docs-bootstrap` gap covering `site.yaml`, the page skeleton, and refgen, instead of one gap per missing piece; every page gap then `depends-on` it. Draft `site.yaml` values (name, tagline, install methods, features) found in README and build files go into that gap's evidence.

## Write the report

Write `docs/.audit.md` per [report-format.md](report-format.md). When a previous report exists, read it first and carry over IDs as that file describes. Done when:

- every check ran, or is listed under `## Not checked` with the reason;
- every gap has every required field, and `action` fits one run of its `fix-by` owner;
- every evidence item cites `path:line`, or a command and its output line, or starts with `unverified:`.

Reply with the report path and the summary line.

## File issues (only when the user asks)

One issue per `open` gap. Read the triage label vocabulary from `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` when present; otherwise use `ready-for-agent` and `needs-triage`. Skip a gap whose title already matches an open issue (`gh issue list --search "<title> in:title"`).

```sh
gh issue create --title "docs: <gap title>" --label <label> --body-file <gap section as a file>
```

Label `ready-for-agent` when `fix-by` is `docs-write`, `docs-bootstrap`, or `refgen` and no evidence is `unverified:`; `needs-triage` otherwise. Record each issue number in its gap as `- issue: #<n>`.
